etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From French émollient, from Latin emolliēns, present active participle of ēmolliō (“make soft”), from ex- + molliō, from mollis (“soft”). By surface analysis, e- +‎ Latin moll- +‎ -i- +‎ -ent.
senses: Something which softens or lubricates the skin; moisturizer.
(figurative) Anything soothing the mind, or that makes something more acceptable.
